text: We evaluated an evolution-strategy refinement method that uses swap-consistency as its fitness signal, with an ES population of 16, transferring supervision from a pythia-410m weak model to a qwen2.5-7b strong model. Across num_seeds = 2 seeds, the weak supervisor reached 0.62 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.83, while the transfer-trained model attained 0.66 accuracy (SE 0.03). The resulting performance gap recovered was 0.18 with a standard error of 0.14, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.21. The measured PGR therefore sits below the baseline, and with only two seeds and a standard error of 0.14 the interval is wide enough that no difference between the method and the baseline can be established in either direction. These numbers should be read as preliminary: two seeds provide little basis for distinguishing method effects from seed-to-seed variation, and additional runs would be needed before drawing any conclusion about the fitness signal's usefulness.
